metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in North Dakota(2026):Rules,Exemptions&Examples

description: North Dakota’s 5% state sales tax applies, but qualifying bullion and covered coins are fully exempt. Jewelry and non-bullion collectibles are taxable.

Sales tax applies
Standard North Dakota sales tax applies at checkout.
What's covered by the exemption
Coins and bullion, especially gold/silver
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in North Dakota.
Is bullion taxable in North Dakota?
+
No. North Dakota fully exempts qualifying bullion from sales tax.
Are gold and silver coins exempt from sales tax in North Dakota?
+
Coins treated as investment bullion/coin purchases are exempt, while non-bullion collectibles can be taxable.
Do I pay sales tax on numismatic coins in North Dakota?
+
It depends. Numismatic items are conditional, and non-bullion collectible items may be taxable.
Is precious-metal jewelry taxable in North Dakota?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable even though bullion and certain coins are exempt.
